source.leg_weights_note: Each leg's junit_source names the CPU run(s) its seconds come from: general legs with selection=not slow and not manual, four workers, dist=loadfile; solution legs with selection=slow, two workers, dist=loadfile. The Linux general legs come from run 39196899855, the Windows general leg from run 39213321138 (one shard, so the report covers the whole leg; it includes three failing seal tests at their recorded seconds), the macOS general leg from both shards of run 39586308373, and the solution legs from runs 37661495008 and 37662436259. Windows takes two general shards. macOS takes four: its three heaviest files are indivisible loadfile atoms of 1653 s (tests/egm/test_finite_negm_public_mixed_corner_family.py), 1329 s (tests/egm/test_finite_negm_public_actual_corner_family.py) and 1311 s (tests/simulation/test_no_feasible_action.py). While the two corner-family files had no macOS weight, they sorted last and both landed in the shard that already held test_no_feasible_action.py, whose four workers then ran three such atoms side by side on the runner's cores; a cold JAX compile cache stretched that shard past the 60-minute job timeout. Four shards give each atom its own shard, which bounds each shard near its largest atom. Root file_weights and frozen_head remain the original reviewer cross-leg CSV and are NOT a per-job basis.
source.batch_4_note: tests/test_simulation_candidate_program_certificate.py and tests/test_uniform_process_grid_certificate.py moved off the four general legs into one Linux/3.14 source-contract lane; tests/test_source_certificate_portability.py is their portability control and stays on every general lane.
source.batch_5_note: general and solution shards are duration-weighted (longest-processing-time over whole-file atoms) from leg_weights; topology lanes are unchained into one step per invocation and never merged.
source.batch_6_note: Rebalanced against measured rather than predicted durations. The batch-5 weights came from run 29396117, whose fp32 legs ran a much smaller selection, so the fp32 general leg was predicted at 79 minutes of worker time and measured at 200, and the fp32 solution leg at 126 against 273. General shards per leg are now 3/2/4/3 (fp64 Linux, fp64 macOS, fp64 Windows, fp32 Linux) and each solution leg takes 7 shards. Windows carries about 8 minutes of per-job setup against 2 on Linux, which is why it takes the most shards for a payload the others carry in fewer.
source.reclassified_slow_note: tests/simulation/test_outer_endpoint_admission.py is marked `slow` at module level and moved from the four general legs to the Linux slow non-solution lanes at both precisions. Its adaptive case peaks at 7.3 GB RSS and was OOM-killed twice as a silent xdist 'node down' on the Windows general shard at four workers; the slow lane runs two workers under --dist loadfile, so the whole module stays on one worker and only one of its cases is ever resident. Nothing about what the module checks changed.
source.initial_conditions_move_note: The initial-condition validation tests moved into tests/simulation/initial_conditions/ (#446). Renamed modules keep the per-file weights observed under their old paths; modules that are new or were split out of an old module carry no observed weight and are listed in unweighted_files until a green run re-measures them.
source.macos_capacity_note: fp64-macos general uses four shards at four workers with macOS-only observed weights from run 39586308373 (see leg_weights_note). Root frozen_head/file_weights, other leg weights/counts and the job payload/total guardrails are unchanged.
source.linux_only_note: linux_only_files lists general-universe files that the macOS and Windows general legs do not run: files with no reasonably expected OS-dependent behaviour (numerics, certificates, kernels), as opposed to paths, file I/O and persistence, process spawning, locale or float formatting and platform dependencies. Files whose classification was uncertain, and numeric files that also hold a save/load/pickle/capture test, stay on every OS. The Linux legs still run every general file. With the reduced universe the macOS and Windows general legs take one shard each; the layout is 4/1/1/4 (fp64 Linux, fp64 macOS, fp64 Windows, fp32 Linux).
source.os_persistence_note: os_persistence_tests are the tests/solution tests whose body writes, reads, pickles or replays on-disk state (save/load_solution, pickle/cloudpickle, h5py, npz, log_path, tmp_path): 214 test functions in 42 files. The whole battery is `slow`, so the macOS and Windows general legs never ran them; tests-os-persistence runs them there by marker at two workers. Their predicted payload uses the Linux fp64 JUnit seconds of the selected cases on run 39196899855 attempt 1 (head c359260bc, 2159 s, largest file 593 s); no macOS or Windows measurement exists, so it is a Linux-measured estimate.
source.certificate_heavy_note: tests/test_final_nested_helper_certificate.py and tests/test_grid_search_candidate_certificate.py left the general universe: each file alone came within 2 minutes of the 30-minute payload guardrail as an indivisible loadfile atom (fp64 1696 s and 1576 s, fp32 1309 s and 1793 s on run 39196899855). tests-certificate-heavy runs both at fp64 and fp32 under --dist load, so their tests spread over two workers; its predicted payload is half their summed leg seconds.
